title: Pascal identity for binomial sums of shifts
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and F\in D(\mathcal O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category]. Put B_n(F)=\bigoplus_{(j,c)\in\coprod_{j=0}^n\operatorname{Fin}(\binom n j)}F[j]. Then F\oplus F[1]\cong B_1(F), and B_n(F)\oplus B_n(F)[1]\cong B_{n+1}(F) for every n\ge0.

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: The index set of B_0 is a singleton and the zero-shift isomorphism identifies B_0 with F. For the successor formula construct the following map from two copies of the index set of B_n to that of B_{n+1}: send an unshifted (j,c) to (j,c), and a shifted (j,c) to (j+1, choose(n,j+1)+c). Pascal's identity makes both maps well-defined.

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: The unshifted entries in target degree j occupy positions below choose(n,j), and the shifted entries occupy the rest. These intervals are disjoint. Invert the map by comparing the target copy number with choose(n,j): the first case has j<=n, and the second has j>0 and comes from j-1. This proves bijectivity, including j=0, j=n+1, and n=0.

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: The shift functor preserves finite biproducts. Distribute it across B_n, identify F[j][1] with F[j+1] using the shift-addition isomorphism, concatenate the two biproducts via their inclusions and projections, and reindex along the preceding bijection. This gives the successor formula. Taking n=0 and using B_0 isomorphic to F gives the initial formula.

mathlib_searches.query: Binomial multiplicity biproduct of shifted objects satisfies Pascal identity
Biproduct of shifts with binomial multiplicities plus its shift is isomorphic to the next binomial biproduct by Pascal identity

lean.statement: theorem binomial_shift_biproduct (Y : Scheme.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))] (F : schemeDerivedCategory Y) : Nonempty (F ⊞ F⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ ≅ biproduct (fun p : (j : Fin 2) × Fin (Nat.choose 1 j.val) ↦ F⟦(p.1.val : ℤ)⟧)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty ((biproduct (fun p : (j : Fin (n + 1)) × Fin (Nat.choose n j.val) ↦ F⟦(p.1.val : ℤ)⟧)) ⊞ (biproduct (fun p : (j : Fin (n + 1)) × Fin (Nat.choose n j.val) ↦ F⟦(p.1.val : ℤ)⟧))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ ≅ biproduct (fun p : (j : Fin (n + 2)) × Fin (Nat.choose (n + 1) j.val) ↦ F⟦(p.1.val : ℤ)⟧)))
